rules_next.rule: Both doctors work the same way
rules_next.detail: mash doctor and mashctl doctor print every row every time, each marked ok, warn, FAIL or skip; a row that cannot run because an earlier one failed is skip, with what it needs. 'checks' in --json always lists every row, whatever failed. After the rows come one blank line and a count ('No problems.', '1 problem, 1 warning.'). A doctor that found a problem always ends with exactly one hint. The hint is a command of ours when one fixes the problem, otherwise one plain sentence naming who or what does. It is never a command that only checks, and never one that replaces credentials, moves a folder or changes permissions unless the doctor found exactly the condition that command fixes. Exit 1 when there is a problem; warnings alone exit 0, or 1 with --strict. A server row shows the address as configured.
rules_next.replaces: Both doctors work the same way

rules_next.rule: Missing credentials read the same in every everyday command
rules_next.detail: When the chosen endpoint's creds file is not where the configuration says: 'error: acme.demo.bob has no credentials here: ~/.config/mash/acme.demo.bob.creds is missing' and 'hint: mash doctor', exit 1, from send, inbox, read and who alike; status says the same as its reason (reason_code creds_missing) and doctor in its creds row. Never the operating system's own wording. A recipient that takes no mail reads 'error: <address> is suspended or was deleted; nothing was sent', hint 'mash who', exit 1; never the server's wording. The sender cannot tell the two apart: all it sees is that no stream took the message, and a recipient deleted while the sender's directory cache still lists it looks the same; a marker in the directory record that tells them apart is planned for 0.6.0. When the set-aside file <address>.creds.deleted is present, send, inbox, read and who say 'error: <address>: this endpoint was deleted; its address cannot be used again' with 'hint: mash doctor', as mash status does.
rules_next.replaces: Missing credentials read the same in every everyday command

rules_next.rule: Encryption can be turned off in one way only, and it says so every time
rules_next.detail: Both tools talk to the server over TLS. The one way to turn that off is the environment variable MASH_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_NATS_ENCRYPTION=1. There is no flag and no configuration-file key for it: this is the one setting that cannot be given three ways, so that it cannot be left on in a file and forgotten. While it is set, every command of both tools, errors included, first prints, on stderr: 'warning: no encryption to the server (MASH_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_NATS_ENCRYPTION)'. The older names, MASH_INSECURE_PLAINTEXT and the key insecure_plaintext, are refused with an error naming the new one.
rules_next.replaces: Encryption can be turned off in one way only, and it says so every time
